keyframe_review.note: 644,005 km2 for 1973-1975, the same cells as the Kingdom's shape. The page gives no area (infobox 'Not stated'); the Kingdom of Afghanistan page gives 652,864 km2 (1973; 652,200 in its text), ratio 0.99. No territorial change in the coup of 17 July 1973; 'By November 1974, Afghanistan began a massive military build-up along the Durand Line.'

Same outline for 1976-1978. After Daoud's talks with Bhutto in June and August 1976 the two countries 'came close to a border deal', stopped by Zia ul-Haq's coup of June 1977; in March 1978 Daoud agreed to stop supporting rebel groups in Pakistan. The republic ended with the Saur Revolution of 27-28 April 1978; the Democratic Republic was established on 30 April.

region.text: the whole country, the kingdom's frontiers

ledger.note: 17 July 1973: Daoud Khan overthrows the king and proclaims the Republic of Afghanistan. Infobox 'Established: 17 July 1973 (coup d'etat)': 'In July 1973, while King Mohammad Zahir Shah ... was in Italy', the coup 'overthrew the Kingdom of Afghanistan and established the Republic of Afghanistan in its place'; a one-party presidential republic.

region.text: the whole country passes to the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan

ledger.note: 27-28 April 1978: the Saur Revolution ends the republic. 'On 27 April, troops from the military base at Kabul International Airport started to move' toward central Kabul; power was consolidated within 24 hours and Daoud was executed the next day; the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan was established on 30 April 1978 under Nur Muhammad Taraki.

wars.name: 1975 Panjshir Valley uprising
belligerents: Islamist rebels in the Panjshir Valley
wars.outcome: A failed rebellion backed by Iran and Pakistan against Daoud's government (the page: 'a failed Iranian-Pakistani backed rebellion sought to oust the government'); no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives the year 1975 (infobox: July) and no detail of the fighting.

wars.name: Saur Revolution
wars.outcome: Army units loyal to the party took Kabul in 24 hours on 27-28 April 1978; Daoud and most of his family were executed; no frontier moved.

certainty.note: The Durand Line was demarcated in 1894-1896 and Afghanistan did not recognise it; nothing on this page changes it. The Iranian (Helmand), Soviet and Chinese frontiers were not checked on this page; the Sino-Afghan delimitation of November 1963 is in the Kingdom's dossier.

notes: One page opened (budget 1-2 pages). The page contains no territorial change; the only frontier items are the 1974 Durand Line military build-up and the 1976-1977 near-agreement with Pakistan, neither of which moved a border. It does not use the term 'Pashtunistan' and does not mention the 1973 Helmand water treaty with Iran, the Chinese frontier, or a February 1977 constitution (it says January 1977, loya jirga). The Democratic Republic of Afghanistan (30 April 1978 to 1987) has no Cliopatria row until the Afghanistan row starts in 1979, so May-December 1978 is covered here by the 1976 shape (end year 1978); the afghanistan dossier (another ia-03 part) should start its own life on 30 April 1978. Neighbours (Cliopatria): Pakistan, Iran (Pahlavi dynasty), India, China (PRC) and the Soviet Union, 1973-1978, all frontier-only.
